name: Validating Nature Images - How Well Each Represents Nature
description: Faithful replication with the paper's own stimuli: participants rate how well each of 129 nature photographs represents nature, on a 5-point scale from 1 (least representing nature) to 5 (best representing nature). The images are the authors' full set from their OSF repository (osf.io/spf8y), which they collected from free image websites to choose stimuli for an fMRI study of nature exposure. Images appear one at a time in random order; one tap rates and moves on. Original study: 40 Texas A&M students; mean rating 4.14 (range 2.73 to 4.88); images with mountains, water or tree canopies were rated higher, and images with man-made elements or close-range views lower. The paper's mean for every image is stored in the page, so a new sample can be compared image by image. Use it to validate a nature stimulus set for your own population before an experiment. Differences from the original study: (1) the images were reduced to at most 1100 px for the web; (2) order is randomised per participant (the paper does not say how it ordered them); (3) the item wording and the age, gender and field questions were written for this template from the paper's description; (4) the OSF set carries no licence statement, and one image credits Texas Parks & Wildlife Department, so check reuse terms before publishing figures with these photos.
author: Menser, Baek, Siahaan, Kolman, Delgado & Kash

config.description: Participants rate 129 photographs of natural scenes, one at a time in random order, on how well each represents nature (1 = least, 5 = best). Rebuilt from Menser, Baek, Siahaan, Kolman, Delgado & Kash (2021), Frontiers in Psychology 12: 685815, with the authors' own image set from OSF (osf.io/spf8y). Analysis: mean rating per image; compare with the paper's means (stored in this page) and with image features (canopies, mountains, water, man-made elements, atmospheric perspective, close-range view).
